data.name: Vanguard V
data.detailed_description:
Join Us On A Journey

as we develop Vanguard V in this Early Access release. This title features the original 2014 prototype level and a completely new level! Level 2 also has developer commentary, simply hit the "Enter" key to get behind-the-scenes info as you play. Also, make sure to check out the Developer Corner to hear from the developers directly in 360 video. Videos are updated alongside the game. Your support will directly help this title reach the finish line!


JackSepticEye playing the 2014 Vanguard V Prototype

Vanguard V

is a fast-paced flight adventure game, designed for Virtual Reality, with diverse settings including flights through space, Earth’s surface, and the worlds below. You are the sole defender and greatest weapon against the Parasites. The freedom of flight meets action adventure! The team includes developers who worked on titles including Uncharted, Shovel Knight, Call of Duty, Syphon Filter, and from a variety of game companies including Sony, Microsoft, EA, Capcom and more!

Reviewers trying out the 2014 Prototype


Qu entering the scene at the start of the all new level 2!


Watch out! Those hurt.


Obsidian Falls

reviews.review:
Vanguard V is an intriguing relic from the earlier years of consumer virtual reality, built around a simple but appealing fantasy: flying freely through science-fiction environments while fighting an extraterrestrial threat. Developed and published by ZeroTransform, it entered Early Access with ambitions of becoming a larger VR action-adventure. What remains today is considerably smaller than that original vision, but the foundation still demonstrates some creative thinking about how speed, movement, and combat can work inside virtual reality.

Instead of placing the player behind the controls of a complicated spacecraft, the game makes flight itself the attraction. You soar through environments while engaging hostile forces known as the Parasites, producing an experience closer to an arcade action game than a realistic flight simulator. This approach makes the controls relatively easy to understand and allows the game to concentrate on movement, spectacle, and the physical sensation of traveling quickly through a three-dimensional space. Players expecting detailed aircraft systems or simulation mechanics should therefore adjust their expectations, as the design is focused much more heavily on immediate VR entertainment.

Environmental variety plays an important role in making the flight mechanics enjoyable. The adventure moves between open space, planetary environments, and more enclosed underground areas. Each setting changes how speed is perceived. Flying across a large open area creates a sense of freedom, while traveling close to terrain or through confined spaces makes obstacles feel considerably more threatening. VR enhances these differences because scale and proximity are much more noticeable when the environment surrounds the player.

Combat gives the flight mechanics a purpose beyond simply exploring scenery. The player must maneuver while attacking enemies and avoiding hazards, creating moments where positioning and awareness become just as important as offensive actions. Vanguard V works best when movement, environmental obstacles, and enemy encounters occur simultaneously. These sequences create the fast arcade rhythm that defines the game and demonstrate why its concept had considerable potential as a full VR adventure.

Unfortunately, the limited amount of content is the game's greatest weakness. Vanguard V remains an Early Access release, and its development did not ultimately produce the complete adventure originally envisioned. The available material includes only a small portion of what could have become a substantially larger campaign. This makes the experience feel more like an extended demonstration of a promising idea than a fully developed action game. Players can experience its mechanics and understand the direction the project was pursuing, but there simply is not enough content to provide the progression, variety, and long-term satisfaction expected from a finished title.

There is nevertheless some historical value in what remains. Developer commentary and behind-the-scenes material provide additional insight into the creation of the project. Vanguard V originated during a period when developers were still experimenting extensively with VR locomotion, comfort, perspective, and control methods. Seen from that perspective, the game becomes an interesting example of early VR design rather than merely an unfinished action title. Its ideas surrounding unrestricted movement and high-speed flight are arguably more memorable than the amount of playable content itself.

The visual presentation similarly benefits from VR more than raw graphical complexity. Large environments, rapid movement, changes in elevation, and objects passing near the player create much of the spectacle. The science-fiction aesthetic supports the straightforward story without overwhelming the action with unnecessary exposition. Its age is apparent when compared with newer VR productions, particularly in environmental detail and overall polish, but the presentation remains functional enough to support the central flying fantasy.

Steam Deck compatibility is effectively unsuitable for normal handheld play. Vanguard V is designed as a VR-only experience requiring compatible PC virtual-reality hardware, so the Steam Deck by itself cannot provide the intended gameplay experience. Even if technical experimentation or external hardware configurations are possible, this should not be mistaken for conventional Steam Deck support. Anyone purchasing specifically for portable Deck gaming should consider the game incompatible with that use case.

Ultimately, Vanguard V is easier to appreciate as an ambitious VR experiment than as a complete commercial adventure. Its combination of high-speed flight, arcade combat, varied environments, and virtual-reality immersion provides glimpses of an exciting concept. The mechanics establish a solid foundation, but the unfinished Early Access state prevents those ideas from developing into the substantial campaign they deserved. For VR enthusiasts interested in older experimental projects, there is some curiosity value here. Players primarily looking for a polished and content-rich action game will find the experience far too limited.

Rating: 6/10
